metaDescription: Generate /.well-known/security.txt with Contact, Expires, Encryption, Policy and Canonical fields, validated against RFC 9116 rules.
intro: Tell security researchers how to report vulnerabilities by publishing a correct security.txt file.
why:
Enter one or more contacts (mailto:, tel: or https: URIs), an expiry date (defaults to one year ahead, since RFC 9116 recommends less than a year) and optional Encryption, Acknowledgments, Policy, Hiring, Preferred-Languages and Canonical fields. The tool validates the URIs and dates and prints the file with a reminder where to host it.

Place the file at /.well-known/security.txt over HTTPS as text/plain, and renew the Expires date before it passes. Optionally clearsign it with PGP.

No data is sent anywhere: the work happens in your browser, so you can use it offline once the page has loaded.
howTo: Enter your security contact and a policy URL if you have one.
Leave Expires blank for one year, or set a date.
Put a reminder in your calendar to renew it.

faq.a: No, but it is a recognised way to receive reports and is checked by some scanners.
So that stale contact details are not trusted. Researchers are told to ignore expired files.

faq.q: Can I use a form instead of email?
faq.a: Yes. Use an https: URL as the Contact value.
No. Everything is processed in your browser, and the page makes no network requests with your input.
